cases.title: Italian escorts shelter a torpedo attack on Pedestal
cases.mission: The 2° and 22° Gruppi escorted the first torpedo formation. The 2° also covered the second. Of 43 torpedo bombers dispatched, 41 reached the convoy at about 13:00.
cases.effect: Mattesini records that the torpedo attack scored no hits. The 109° Gruppo commander ditched under fighter attack and the 2° Gruppo lost a Re.2001.
cases.limit: The two formations shared escorts. This reconstruction does not isolate how much damage the fighters prevented or determine outcomes of the other air attacks that day.

cases.title: Fighters cover Ohio while the convoy reaches port
cases.mission: From 05:30 No. 249 Squadron covered convoy ships. Eight Spitfires of No. 185 Squadron guarded the incoming tanker Ohio from 06:43 to 08:16.
cases.effect: The Vice-Admiral at Malta reported fuel discharged by 09:00 on 16 August from Ohio and four merchant ships. The naval damage return puts Ohio’s arrival at 10:00 on 15 August and records a broken upper deck and flooded spaces.
cases.limit: The fighter patrol ending at 08:16 and the naval arrival at 10:00 mark different observations. The port signal combines cargoes from five ships. It cannot say which fuel came from Ohio or which attack a patrol prevented.

Allied.effort: Nos. 185 and 249 supplied timed approach patrols on 15 August. Indomitable’s campaign return covers a separate carrier effort.
Allied.losses: Indomitable reported eight aircraft lost and four pilots saved during Pedestal. On Malta, two No. 229 Spitfires were damaged in a landing collision on 15 August.
Allied.effect: The port’s 16 August signal records unloading from five ships including Ohio. The island patrols document cover during the approach.

Axis.effort: The Italian 13:00 wave on 12 August sent 43 torpedo aircraft. Two turned back. Two fighter groups provided escort.
Axis.losses: The Italian account identifies the 109° commander’s ditched S.79 and one 2° Gruppo Re.2001 shot down.
Axis.effect: Mattesini found no torpedo hit from this wave. Other attacks on the convoy continued and the ship damage return does not assign every hit to a unit.

cases.title: Beach cover flew from Malta before the move to Pachino
cases.mission: No. 92 Squadron flew 42 sorties on 10 July covering the Pachino beaches from Malta. On 13 July eleven pilots patrolled en route to Pachino and landed there. On 14 July the squadron flew two patrols before its ground personnel arrived.
cases.effect: The squadron recorded an attack on Ju 88s over the landing area on the 10th and contact with Italian fighters after moving ashore. Pilot Dicks-Sherwood, missing on the 10th, returned after a trawler picked him up. The diary later confirmed Savage died.
cases.limit: The 41 sorties on 13 July include flying either side of the change of base. The surviving patrol figures do not provide a number of bombers prevented from reaching the beaches.

cases.title: US fighter-bombers reached Milazzo harbour
cases.mission: The XII Air Support Command daily summary records 36 A-36s bombing Milazzo harbour on 25 July. Its basing table lists the 27th and 86th Bombardment Groups as dive-bomber groups.
cases.effect: Crews reported a direct hit on a merchant ship and near misses on small craft. The operational summary shows the effort against a port still supporting the Axis.
cases.limit: The summary gives no ship name and no group-by-group allocation of the 36 aircraft. Vessel damage and interruption at the port need a harbour or ship record.

cases.title: Ferry damage forced traffic away from the Salvatore jetty
cases.mission: At 07:25 on 16 August eight No. 92 Squadron pilots covered 12 Warhawks attacking shipping. Six later escorted 12 Baltimores to Messina. A separate afternoon patrol covered warships southeast of Taormina.
cases.effect: Captain von Liebenstein recorded a near miss badly damaging ferry barge F 607 and damage to two Siebel ferries shortly before 16:00. Bombing disabled the Salvatore jetty. A reserve embarkation point kept the service operating. The last ferries left Messina shortly before 06:00 on 17 August.
cases.limit: Neither diary identifies the bombers responsible for F 607. For SF 175 the translation places its grounding sequence under the night of 15/16 August. The craft register dates it to 23:00 on the 16th and also cites the transport diary. SF 92 helped recover its load. No. 92 Squadron’s record establishes escort and patrol.

Allied.effort: No. 92 recorded 42 sorties from Malta on 10 July and 41 on the transition day of 13 July. The US command separately reported 36 A-36s against Milazzo on 25 July.
Allied.losses: The squadron recorded two missing pilots on 10 July, then a trawler rescue and one confirmed death. On 16 August it recorded Brendan Baker missing from a separate escort.
Allied.effect: Pachino patrols operated before the ground party arrived. At Messina the diary identifies escorted strike formations, but the German ferry damage lacks an attacking unit.

Axis.effort: The 10 July strength table distinguishes island and mainland or Sardinian Gruppen, plus night and ground-attack forces. It supplies no sorties by unit.
Axis.losses: The ferry diary identifies F 607 and two damaged Siebel ferries on 16 August. SF 175’s wrecking time differs between the translated night entry and the craft register.
Axis.effect: Bombing closed the Salvatore jetty. The ferry command shifted embarkation and finished its final crossings the following morning.

cases.title: Carrier patrols sustained cover while Montecorvino was under fire
cases.mission: Force V began Seafire patrols at 06:15 on 9 September and flew 265 sorties that day across five carriers. On Attacker, 886 Naval Air Squadron was among the units flying. Its pilot P. B. N. Prentice was killed on approach to the carrier.
cases.effect: The US Army recorded that German artillery still denied use of Montecorvino on 10–11 September, leaving air support to carriers and distant Sicilian bases. No. 324 Wing moved to Tusciano on the 12th. The Army dates completion of the new strip near Paestum to the 13th.
cases.limit: The patrol count covers all five carriers. Neither the army account nor the movement timetable identifies the ship or troops protected by an individual 886 Squadron sortie.

cases.title: A German strike forced USS Savannah off the gun line
cases.mission: On the morning of 11 September III./KG 100 attacked the US cruisers in the Gulf of Salerno. The naval chronology names 16 aircraft in the attacking formation.
cases.effect: USS Savannah was supporting troops ashore when a bomb hit turret three. A contemporary photograph shows the damage and fire. The US Army recorded that the cruiser had to withdraw from its fire-support position.
cases.limit: The German formation count covers attacks on more than one ship. The ship photograph and army account cannot identify which crew made the hit or which fighter patrol was nearest.

cases.title: The air command redirected Mustangs toward Eighth Army’s front
cases.mission: On 11 September Desert Air Force ordered No. 239 Wing’s Mustangs off long-range reconnaissance so they could support the army and attack communications closer to the front.
cases.effect: In its account of the fighting on 14–15 September, the RAF history records army reports that attacks on troop concentrations, gun positions and strongpoints eased the advance. Some pilots could not locate guns reported by the troops.
cases.limit: The army assessment covers the broader air effort. It cannot isolate No. 239 Wing’s contribution or assign the capture of a particular position to its aircraft. The US transfers on 15 and 20 September were administrative changes.

cases.title: Fighter-bombers supported the Senio crossing
cases.mission: The South African account places fighter-bombers of Nos. 7 and 8 Wings, No. 5 Squadron, No. 3 Wing’s medium bombers and No. 40 Squadron’s army-cooperation aircraft in the offensive that opened on 9 April.
cases.effect: The Canadian Army history describes fighter-bomber and medium-bomber attacks between artillery bombardments before Eighth Army troops crossed the Senio that evening. By the morning of 12 April, assaulting divisions had gained a foothold across the next river, the Santerno.
cases.limit: The ground account describes a combined attack by several air forces alongside artillery and infantry. It gives no squadron-to-company match. South African night operations and later April sorties have a wider time window.

Allied.losses: 886 Squadron lost Sub-Lt Prentice on approach to Attacker. The Force V account records 32 aircraft written off across the carrier operation.
Allied.effect: Offshore cover remained necessary while artillery denied Montecorvino. A new strip near Paestum went into service on 13 September. By April 1945 fighter-bombers were participating in the Senio offensive.

Axis.effort: On 9 September the German return records 82 fighter sorties and 26 ground-attack sorties. Separate German and Republican Italian returns give strengths for 20 August 1944.
Axis.losses: The 12 September naval chronology records one aircraft lost from the II./KG 100 attack. No comparable German loss total for all Salerno fighters is established here.
Axis.effect: On 11 September III./KG 100’s attack forced Savannah to withdraw from supporting the landing force. The later fighter strength tables alone cannot establish effects over the ground front.
